pride_data.title: Proteomic profiling of a healthy biological sample (human serum) obtained from the surface of the AFM chip.
pride_data.projectDescription: Mass spectrometric analysis was used to identify proteins from a biological plasma samples covalently immobilized on the surface of an AFM chip using cross-linkers SuccBB.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Trypsinolysis Protocol:  Preparation of Reaction Mixture: To initiate trypsinolysis, prepare a solution containing:  10 µl of trypsin (concentration: 0.1 g/l) 50 µl of TEAB (50 mM) 1000 µl of deionized water Add this solution to tubes containing the AFM chips, ensuring that the solution completely covers the mica surface.  Incubation: Place the tubes with AFM chips in a shaker-incubator and incubate for 18 hours at 37°C, with agitation at 140 rpm.  Mixing: After incubation, transfer the tubes to a shaker for 60 minutes at 800 rpm and 40°C to ensure proper mixing.  Centrifugation: Subsequently, mix the tubes on a Vortex for 1 minute, then centrifuge for 10 minutes at 9000 rpm.  Post-centrifugation Procedure: Using tweezers, remove the AFM chips from the tube containing the tryptic mixture. Wash each side of the chips with 40 µl of acetonitrile using a laboratory dispenser. Collect the wash into the test tube with the tryptic lysate. Add an additional 40 µl of acetonitrile to the inside of the tube lid and close the tube.  Centrifugation: Centrifuge the tubes again for 10 minutes at 9000 rpm.  Panoramic Mass Spectrometry: For panoramic mass spectrometry analysis, use the Q Exactive™ HF Hybrid Quadrupole-Orbitrap™ mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Rockwell, IL, USA). This instrument is capable of performing panoramic protein searches and is widely used in routine proteomic analyses.  Peptide Separation: Peptides from each sample are separated using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) with the Ultimate 3000 Nano LC System (Thermo Scientific, Rockwell, IL, USA). A 15 cm long, 75 µm id C18 column (Acclaim® PepMap™ RSLC, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Rockwell, IL, USA) is used for separation.  Peptides are eluted with a gradient of 5–35% buffer B (80% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid) over 115 minutes at a flow rate of 0.3 µl/min. The total run time includes:  90 minutes to reach 99% buffer B 10 minutes of washing with 99% buffer B 15 minutes of re-equilibration with buffer A (0.1% formic acid).
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: For each sample, the raw Q Exactive™ mass spectrometer data (RAW files) were processed using MaxQuant software (version 1.5.5.1, Jürgen Cox, Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry, Martinsried, Germany), with the integrated Andromeda search engine. Bioinformatics analysis was then performed using the Perseus program (version 2.0.6.0, Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry, Germany).  For each sample, mass spectrometric data were analyzed by comparing the area under the peak of the parent ion, followed by the calculation of IBQ values using the built-in algorithm in MaxQuant.
keywords: Protein immobilization; atomic force microscopy; crosslinker; mass spectrometry
